extracted.intended_audience: educated readers and policymakers interested in political philosophy, public finance, and the French Revolution
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted evaluative principles and standards embedded in Edmund Burke's political essay about government, public finance, and revolutionary reform. These are criteria Burke uses to judge policies, leaders, and constitutional change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve public revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: The revenue will not be trifled with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government must not treat public revenue lightly or adopt expedient tricks; fiscal measures that undermine or toy with the revenue (e.g., fanciful schemes of paper circulation or mercantile contrivances) are condemned as dangerous and fraudulent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual relief must be effective, not rhetorical
rubrics_metrics.description: They did not relieve the people. If they entertained such intentions, why did they order the obnoxious taxes to be paid? The people relieved themselves, in spite of the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate relief measures by their real effects on the people (did they reduce burdens or merely provide appearance of relief?). Beware leaders who claim benevolence while policy actions (like continuing hated taxes) show otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid alchemy/illusory finance
rubrics_metrics.description: I mean the project for coining into money the bells of the suppressed churches. This is their alchemy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject fanciful or symbolic financial schemes that have no solid basis. Practical, credible financial resources are required; schemes that trade on spectacle or symbolism (here, coining church bells) are anti-patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on mercantile contrivances to replace order
rubrics_metrics.description: All their drawing and re-drawing, on their circulation for putting off the evil day, on the play between the Treasury and the Caisse d'Escompte, and on all these old, exploded contrivances of mercantile fraud, now exalted into policy of state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial instruments and maneuvers are only useful when built upon settled public order; using them as a substitute for sound political foundations is misguided and will fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy judged by balance of taxation and benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it be more advantageous to the people to pay considerably and to gain in proportion, or to gain little or nothing and to be disburdened of all contribution? My mind is made up to decide in favor of the first proposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating reforms, prefer solutions where subjects pay taxes but receive proportionate benefits, rather than schemes that avoid contribution but yield little advantage. The balance between contributions and gains is a core political test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain balance between acquisition and state demands
rubrics_metrics.description: To keep a balance between the power of acquisition on the part of the subject and the demands he is to answer on the part of the state is the fundamental part of the skill of a true politician.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good government calibrates taxation and obligations so as not to destroy incentives to acquire wealth; protecting the ability to acquire is politically prior and necessary for prosperity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good order as foundational
rubrics_metrics.description: Good order is the foundation of all good things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All reforms and financial devices must rest on a settled order; disturbance of that order undermines any subsequent policy benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for magistrates and laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The magistrate must have his reverence, the laws their authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social stability requires deference to lawful authority; reform should not root out principles of natural subordination or erode respect for legal institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect property and labor
rubrics_metrics.description: They must respect that property of which they cannot partake. They must labor to obtain what by labor can be obtained; and when they find, as they commonly do, the success disproportioned to the endeavor, they must be taught their consolation in the final proportions of eternal justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies should encourage labor and respect existing property rights; removing respect for property or promising easy access to others' holdings kills industry and acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid policies that expose industry to plunder
rubrics_metrics.description: Of this consolation whoever deprives them deadens their industry, and strikes at the root of all acquisition as of all conservation. He that does this is the cruel oppressor... by his wicked speculations he exposes the fruits of successful industry and the accumulations of fortune to the plunder of the negligent, the disappointed, and the unprosperous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticizes reforms that unsettle property or encourage redistribution by force/abuse—such measures punish industry and encourage plunder by the unsuccessful; evaluate reforms for their effect on property security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial skill must be grounded in settled order
rubrics_metrics.description: Too many of the financiers by profession are apt to see nothing in revenue but banks, and circulations, and annuities on lives, and tontines, and perpetual rents... They are good, but then only good when they assume the effects of that settled order, and are built upon it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical financial expertise is valuable only when political and social order is preserved; finance cannot substitute for political foundations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not excuse incapacity with lofty rhetoric
rubrics_metrics.description: The effects of the incapacity shown by the popular leaders in all the great members of the commonwealth are to be covered with the 'all-atoning name' of Liberty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware leaders who cloak incompetence or harmful acts under the name of liberty; rhetoric should not shield poor governance from critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberty requires wisdom and virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: What is liberty without wisdom and without virtue? It is the greatest of all possible evils; for it is folly, vice, and madness, without tuition or restraint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate claims to liberty alongside the presence of wisdom and virtue; unbridled liberty lacking moral and intellectual guidance is dangerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forming a free government requires sagacity
rubrics_metrics.description: To form a free government, that is, to temper together these opposite elements of liberty and restraint in one consistent work, requires much thought, deep reflection, a sagacious, powerful, and combining mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating a stable free government is hard and demands capable, reflecting leadership able to balance liberty and restraint—this is a standard when judging revolutionaries or constitutional designers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaders must not pander to popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: When the leaders choose to make themselves bidders at an auction of popularity, their talents, in the construction of the state, will be of no service. They will become flatterers instead of legislators,--the instruments, not the guides of the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique of political behavior: leaders who seek popularity at all costs abandon statesmanship. Evaluate leaders by whether they legislate with courage and moderation rather than pandering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value moderation and compromise as political virtues
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderation will be stigmatized as the virtue of cowards, and compromise as the prudence of traitors,--until... the popular leader is obliged to become active in propagating doctrines and establishing powers that will afterwards defeat any sober purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns that public opinion may vilify moderation, but preserving moderation and willingness to compromise are essential to building stable institutions; evaluate political culture for its tolerance of moderation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conserve useful traditions when reforming
rubrics_metrics.description: I would make the reparation as nearly as possible in the style of the building... Let us add, if we please, but let us preserve what they have left; and standing on the firm ground of the British Constitution, let us be satisfied to admire, rather than attempt to follow in their desperate flights, the aëronauts of France.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reforms should aim to preserve and repair in continuity with existing constitutional and cultural forms rather than radical, imitative, or revolutionary reconstructions; prefer conservative, stylistically consistent change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate superficial improvements from fundamental errors
rubrics_metrics.description: The improvements of the National Assembly are superficial, their errors fundamental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing reforms, test whether changes are merely superficial fixes or whether they introduce profound, structural errors; superficial gains do not justify fundamental damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge policy by concrete accounts and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: The reader is capable of judging, by the aggregate of these immense charges, on the state and condition of France, and the system of public economy adopted in that nation. These articles of account produced no inquiry or discussion in the National Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial transparency and public accounting are criteria for assessing the state's health; lack of inquiry into large expenditures is a failing that undermines trust and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware transformative zeal that insists on total destruction
rubrics_metrics.description: "Tous les établissemens en France couronnent le malheur du peuple: pour le rendre heureux, il faut le renouveler, changer ses idées, changer ses loix, changer ses mœurs, ... tout détruire; oui, tout détruire; puisque tout est à récréer_."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques absolute revolutionary doctrines that advocate destroying all institutions; such maximalist prescriptions are presented as dangerous and a criterion for alarm when judging revolutionary programs.
